---
title: "Backends"
---

Run the same pipeline in memory, in a database, or in Polars. Every table method is
part of the `Phibble\Contracts\Table` interface, and three classes implement
it:

| Backend | Class | Runs | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| In memory | `Phibble\DataFrame` | PHP arrays | Small and medium data, closures, anything |
| SQL | `Phibble\Sql\SqlTable` | SQLite, PostgreSQL, or MySQL | Data that lives in a database |
| Polars | `Phibble\Polars\PolarsTable` | Polars, through the php_polars extension from [phpolars](https://github.com/phpstats/phpolars) | Large data in memory |

Code written against `Table`, including phplyr's functions, runs on any of them.
A backend that cannot run a step exactly, such as a PHP closure or a function
with no exact translation, loads its rows into PHP and runs the step in a
`DataFrame`. Later steps also run in memory. Results match `DataFrame` with
these exceptions:

- A database cannot represent some of R's values, such as `NaN` in MySQL. The
  [SQL tables](sql.qmd#known-differences) page lists these cases.
- Rows from a SQL join, and from a SQL table without `arrange()`, come back
  in the order the database returns them.
- Floating-point results can differ in the last digits. The SQL and Polars
  tests compare floats rounded to nine decimal places.

The [Table contract](contract.qmd) page states the rules each backend follows.

## Choosing and switching

```php
use Phibble\DataFrame;

use function Phibble\{tbl, polars};
use function Phibble\Expr\{col, mean, n};

$df = DataFrame::fromCsv(
    'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/datasets/main/csv/weather.csv'
);
$sql = tbl($pdo, 'weather');
$fast = polars($df);

$summary = fn ($t) => $t
    ->filter(col('temp')->isNa()->not())
    ->groupBy(['origin'])
    ->summarize(['n' => n(), 'temp' => mean(col('temp'))]);

$summary($df);
$summary($sql)->collect();
$summary($fast)->collect();
```

- On `$sql`, the summary runs as one SQL query.
- `collect()` turns any table into a `DataFrame`. `polars()` and
  `PolarsTable::fromTable()` move a table into Polars, and `tbl()` opens a
  database table or query.
- The `Table` interface declares only `summarise()`. Code that accepts any
  `Table` should call it, although all three classes also have `summarize()`.

## The Polars backend

`PolarsTable` loads only when used, so phibble runs without the extension.

- Expressions, joins (including `join_by` comparisons and rolling joins),
  pivots, and the lubridate and stringr functions run in Polars.
- Steps it cannot run, such as PHP closures and `str_to_title()`, run in a
  `DataFrame`. `PolarsTable::$fallbacks` counts them.
- `PolarsTable::$strict = true` throws `PolarsFallback` instead, naming the
  method and the reason.

Type mapping:

- A time column is a Polars duration in microseconds, which, like an hms, can
  be negative or longer than a day. A Polars `Time` column reads as a time.
- Comparisons of times, `is_na()`, `min()`, `max()`, `first()`, and `last()`
  run in Polars. Other functions of a time run in a `DataFrame`, as do
  `sum()`, `mean()`, `median()`, `quantile()`, `sd()`, `var()`, and `iqr()` of
  dates and datetimes.
- `fromTable()` throws on a list-column of named arrays with different keys,
  since Polars structs have every key in every row, and on a list-column of
  `DataFrame`s.

The Polars test suite runs phibble's dplyr, tidyr, lubridate, and stringr
reference cases on `PolarsTable` and skips when the extension is not loaded.
